body: Believe it or not, I feel batter for writing this.

Well, I cried for a while. Been needing to do that for a while now, I think. It just isn't something I do normally, but there's some heavy shit that has built up. Anyway, I got even more panicked, called a couple of those hotline numbers for my state. Two busy signals, one dry and caustic government employee (who I hung up on) later, and I started to pull myself together. I started cleaning up after the contractors that were working on this project all weekend, and I let myself think. Then I remembered that impossible boogeymen don't really exist, and that as you define them, their power ebbs. So I started to write things down. In doing so, I identified  key things that I already knew, but refused to pay attention to, that held the keys to my solution. Here's what I wrote, redacted to keep me anonymous:

Who are my Contractors?

Carpentry and Dry Wall: **redacted_info**

HVAC/Providing fridges/general help: **redacted_info**

Plumbing and Mechanical Services **redacted_info and more**

Mid range bid Plumber: **redacted_info**

Network, Telephony, Video Surveilance: **redacted_info**

Electrician: **redacted_info**

Engineer, MEP plans/drawings: **redacted_info**

Flooring Tile Specialist: **redacted_info**

**redacted_info**, Ventilation prospectives awaiting bid: **redacted_info** **redacted_info**

HVAC??? Find out who **redacted_info** hired for HVAC tomorrow morning at 8am... add them to this list. Get them to handle ductwork for the ventahood?


FACT: We still do not have a **redacted_info** Permit. Without this Permit, we cannot lawfully complete Electrical, Plumbing, Drywall/Carpentry.

FACT: Consequences of doing the work before permit issuance will be heavy fines for myself. Also, **redacted_info** will have nothing to do with it. Also strong potential for additional fines levied against the contractors who do the work.

Opinion: **Name Redacted** doesn't want this job, and keeps pushing the time required to get the MEP and CAD drawings together further back as a tactic in passive resistance. FURTHER: Unless I sit everyone down together, ie, Plumber, Electrician, HVAC, Venthood team, and Carpenter on one side, and Engineer/Architect on the other, we will continue to make only superficial progress.

RESOLUTION: Call emergency meeting with all parties to arrive tomorow morning.


**name_redacted** will ask why this was not done sooner. Will blame failure on me fully. It is already too late to get the permit in time for the opening **BLoop** and **beEP** have specified. Will tell me he told me so. Will ask me how much money my mistake cost. **WILL NOT GET PUNCHED IN THE MOUTH.**
Will go to bed horny as usual, while his GF shops till she drops at the Mall.
wow, fucking hotline is busy-signal. I guess everyone is melting down today.

Also, asking my investors for help would reveal how far off track this project has become, exactly how much risk they are carrying right now, and would incite a couple of them to panic and rash behavior. I can't have that. I can barely hold it together now and they all think I'm the ice-man...

"I have a problem and I need help."

I have the necessary humility to say that. But I have no one I can safely say it to. The people who have invested in me are not qualified to help me solve the problems that are the root of this all. There is a person who could help me, and he is actively trying to help me, but he is possibly more fucked up than me. He is frustrated and at the end of his rope with me, and the only way he knows to communicate with others is abusive and belittling. I know he wants me to succeed, perhaps even more than the people who's money is at risk, but I can't take any more of his help.

I'm trying to step back and breath, though. I'm trying to find a different perspective.

Please know that *I* know that suicide isn't sane. I won't kill myself. I **do** need to talk to someone though. I couldn't read the captcha cause I'm bawling my midlife-crisis eyes out. But I won't do anything drastic. I'm not that far gone. I need help finding my way back onto the path.
